content.text:
I changed `DefaultBruteForceProtector.processLogin` in `services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/managers/DefaultBruteForceProtector.java`. I haven't compiled it or run `BruteForceTest`, and I haven't reproduced the flake. The change is a three-line edit.

The failure time was being read with `Time.currentTimeMillis()` inside the queued async job, so it depended on when the job ran. `testExceedMaxTemporaryLockouts` moves the time offset (`timeOffSet.set(21)`, then `42`) right after a login. A job that ran late could therefore record its failure with the shifted clock, and the lockout would be computed from the wrong time. The result would be the wrong login event, which fits the "Expected error event" assertion.

The time is now captured when the login happens, before the job is submitted, and passed into `failure(...)`. I didn't touch the tests.

This is my best explanation, not a confirmed one. The test also never waits for the async brute-force queue, and I didn't change that.
